# Person-affiliation review evidence

The [fresh interpretation-model trial](./mention-model-v1/README.md) retains three
new official-page excerpts and six synthetic controls. Automatic proposals stay
separate from literal source anchors and reviewed semantics; failures are retained,
not repaired or promoted to affiliations.

These are complete retained public source bodies and reviewed test annotations,
not a runtime identity whitelist. See the
[corpus contract and observed results](../../../docs/design/person-affiliation-corpus.md).

The [additional sample capture](./discovery-sample-v1/capture.json) was generated by
`enrich-affiliations --sample-size 3` on 2026-09-16. Generic hash selection from the
retained FEC filing chooses three exact name/employer pairs outside the reviewed
pairs; no person annotations or expected QIDs drive the requests. Nine search windows
completed successfully. All three appearances retain no corresponding-name candidate
in those windows, which is a coverage gap rather than a verified identity negative.
The manifest pins full public response bodies and safe selected headers. Source
attribution is retained in each request URL; Wikimedia item bodies are CC0 evidence.
See the [automated report](../../../docs/design/affiliation-enrichment.md) for scope,
selection, measured results and replay commands. Earlier fixtures are unchanged.

The later [supplementary-source snapshots](./supplementary-v1/README.md) retain four
HTML pages and one official licensing PDF discovered through interactive research
on those same appearances. They test the existing lexical reader and preserve
source/identity/time gaps; they do not provide an automatic discovery feed or
replace the original source corpus.

The [prose evaluation fixtures](./prose-evaluation-v1/README.md) retain a later fixed
selection outside the grammar's development pages. They preserve failed retrieval
and missed role witnesses as test results, without tuning the parser or asserting
donations by the newly selected page subjects.

The [local-model trial](./prose-model-v1/README.md) adds complete public-source
requests/responses and offline citation replay. Manual excerpt selection and semantic
review remain explicit; model output is not accepted affiliation or identity data.
The [stronger-model trial](./prose-model-gpt-oss-v1/README.md) retains the same
fourteen cases and task with supported GPT-OSS controls. Both runs replay offline;
more literal passes do not erase semantic/context failures.
The [entry-attachment trial](./prose-attachment-v1/README.md) changes that output
contract separately: Go retains original text and full supplied context. It includes
nine new synthetic controls and preserves role/pronoun/retraction failures without
repairing model output or accepting affiliations.
The [mention/interpretation fixtures](./mention-interpretation-v1/README.md) are
explicitly reviewed annotations over retained synthetic cases. They test source
preservation and conditional context rules, not improved model extraction.

`corpus.json` pins every input by SHA-256 and byte count. Do not edit source bytes;
retain a new snapshot and version the corpus when evidence changes. The exact
Schedule A layout is copied from the existing source contract; a regression test
also verifies that it still matches that contract.

The FEC document and headers are exact copies of report 1730162 already retained
by the 2026-09-10 receipt-memo review. They are as-filed source evidence, not a new
processed ledger. The complete file includes public filing contact/address fields;
tests and diagnostic results do not print those fields. The company HTML pages
were fetched for this bounded review on 2026-09-15. They are research snapshots,
not normal Go capture manifests or an implemented automatic refresh process.
No operator contact or credential-bearing request metadata is included.

Cases were selected during development: two occurrences with one reported
name/employer, a second executive-looking appearance, and a reported engineer
without external discovery. This is neither representative sampling nor a held-out
accuracy test. Selection by reported occupation here does not define runtime
leadership, identity or donor eligibility.

`reviewed_roles` contains manually interpreted source assertions. Excerpts and
their generated byte locators make that review inspectable. They do not make role
classification, identity grouping or date interpretation automatic. Role IDs and
`review:` subject IDs must never become production lookup rules. The current
corpus intentionally supplies no day-level role validity that its sources do not
establish. An absent external candidate is not evidence that a person has no role.

Sources and attribution:

- [Federal Election Commission report 1730162](https://docquery.fec.gov/dcdev/posted/1730162.fec).
- [JC2 Ventures team](https://www.jc2ventures.com/about).
- [JC2 Ventures biography](https://www.jc2ventures.com/john-chambers).
- [Ridgeline leadership](https://ridgeline.ai/company/leadership).

Replay offline through `go test ./internal/audit/personaffiliation`. No network,
live database, local model or private credentials are required by these tests.

The later [source-attempt record](./role-source-attempts.json) and three `wikidata-maxlag`
JSON bodies retain failed bounded Wikidata observations. They are separate from the
unchanged corpus manifest. Tests reject them as API errors rather than empty role
sets. Full response headers remain private; the shared attempt record contains only
selected safe metadata, not a substitute exact-header artifact. The
[structured-role reader](../../../docs/design/wikidata-role-extraction.md) also passes
the subsequently retained [interactive observation](./role-source-interactive.json).
Its complete `wikidata-interactive-1.json` body is public CC0 Wikidata evidence;
request metadata explains the user-approved interactive exception. Background
capture policy is unchanged. The offline comparison preserves one historical-role
agreement and title/discovery gaps, not accepted FEC identities. Neither role
annotations nor FEC appearances were rewritten. Test-only subject correspondences
must not become runtime identity lookup rules.

The separate [discovery-v1 capture](./discovery-v1/capture.json) records the later
automatic nine-search plan generated from the same four FEC appearances. It retains
complete public responses and safe selected headers only. No cookies, private
operator contact or request-network metadata are included. Wikipedia search evidence
is attributed through exact request URLs and page revisions; Wikidata item statements
are public CC0 evidence. See the [discovery contract and measured gaps](../../../docs/design/affiliation-discovery.md).
This capture does not replace the reviewed corpus or approve any donor identity.

The separate [discovery-v2 capture](./discovery-v2/capture.json) retains fifteen
searches from the same source appearances, including all baseline query texts and
explained employer variants. It is independently timed, not a replacement for v1.
All responses passed; the added variants failed to recover the missing companies.
Tests preserve the observed namesake and non-company alias counterexamples. Shared
fixtures again contain only safe headers and public bodies. Neither reviewed labels
nor expected QIDs generate queries or control runtime name matching.

The [GLEIF name capture](./gleif-names-v1/capture.json) contains three employer-only
queries from the same verified FEC appearances. It is independent of the Wikipedia
results and requires no prior LEI. Complete public responses and safe headers
retain two corresponding-name LEIs as ambiguous; empty query windows are not
company absence. See the [registry discovery result](../../../docs/design/organization-registry-discovery.md).
No reviewed role label, manually selected company page or expected identity drives
these requests, and no person-role assertion is extracted from registry names.

The [company-page reader](../../../docs/design/company-page-evidence.md) now tests
automatic lexical extraction directly against the three unchanged HTML files.
Test expectations do not enter runtime code. Exact spans and original source text
remain distinct from reviewed roles, person identity and historical validity.

The separate [dated-role review](./dated-roles/review.json) pins two additional
complete public HTML snapshots collected on 2026-09-16: a Sprinklr proxy and a
Ridgeline announcement. Requested/final URLs and hashes preserve the research
provenance; these are not production HTTP capture manifests. Source-date meanings
and role points are reviewed annotations, not automatic prose interpretation or
continuous service. The [evidence check](../../../docs/audit/dated-person-role-evidence-2026-09-16.md)
records the tests and the additional web-only Workday comparison. No source from
the original corpus or prior discovery captures was replaced.
